title: The Nottingham Corpus of Early Modern German Midwifery and Women's Medicine, ca. 1500–1700 (GeMi, OTA 2562)
notes: Whitt's GeMi corpus (OTA 2562, published 2016) holds 12 German midwifery and women's-medicine texts ca. 1500–1700 (Rösslin's Rosengarten, the anonymous Frauenbüchlein ca. 1500, Rüff's Trostbüchlein, HoffWeheMutter, HebammenBuch...) in paired RAW plain-text and TEI XML files plus a manual — the RAW/TEI file pairs with dates match the harvest origins one-for-one ('GeMi: FrauenbüchleinRAW (1500)', 'GeMi: RosengartenRAW (1513)', 'GeMi: JungfrawenRAW (1624)'; 12 distinct origin files = the 12 corpus texts). Transcriptions derive mostly from the Würzburg 'Digitale Volltexte' Gynäkologie collection; CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Caveat: OTA pages sit behind an Anubis anti-bot proof-of-work gate (HTTP 200 but challenge page to crawlers); open the URL in a browser. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the RQ Open Corpus snapshot v2026.06 (in-core, deduplicated texts).
institution: University of Nottingham (Richard J. Whitt), deposited at the Oxford Text Archive (ota:2562)
